title: The standard approach: cut along a curve and glue surfaces with corners
body:
## Note

The standard approach to proving that scl is rational for an arbitrary chain C in the
fundamental group of a closed hyperbolic surface S. Choose a simple essential curve gamma
on S and cut along it. This decomposes the chain C into a collection of arcs
in the cut-open surface, whose fundamental group is free.

One then looks for surfaces with corners in the cut-open surface which glue together
along gamma to give an admissible surface for C.

This is the natural generalisation of the argument that settles the case where C can be
made disjoint from some simple essential curve. In that case the cut-open surface already
contains the whole of C, its fundamental group is free, and no gluing is needed at all.
The reason the general case is hard is recorded separately.
author: danny
